args.rationale: Applying the firm's UCC Article 2 scope memo to Contract 2 (Ferrand & Slate advisory engagement): the contract's entire subject is the performance of consulting/advisory/design labor — studying and redesigning Halcyon's warehouse picking workflow, delivering a written recommendations report, and coaching floor supervisors through implementation, for a $54,000 professional fee. Under Section 2 of the memo, a contract whose entire subject is the performance of labor, consulting, design, or advisory work is governed by the common law, even where the service provider incidentally delivers paper or other trivial materials. Here Ferrand & Slate sells no equipment and transfers title to nothing except the paper report embodying its advice, which is a trivial material incident to the services and does not create an Article 2 sale. Contract 2 contains no goods price allocation, so the Section 3 hybrid/predominant-purpose test does not apply; even on a dominant-thrust analysis the engagement is services. The common law governs Contract 2, and the determination is recorded as the negative disposition (rejected).

For hybrids, the predominant-purpose test applies (per price allocation, if >half the price is goods, entire contract is Article 2).
